question: What is a major safety worry when a nurse has to manually remove a hard stool impaction with gloved fingers?

options.A: Immediate development of permanent bowel incontinence
options.B: Sudden severe spikes in the patient's blood pressure
options.C: Stimulation of the vagus nerve causing bradycardia
options.D: Accidental puncture of the abdominal wall muscles

explanation: Be careful here! Messing around in the rectum can trigger the vagus nerve, causing a sudden drop in heart rate. Always keep an eye on your patient's pulse. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h4)

question: A rural health clinic has only two nurses on duty. Which staffing approach ensures the best care for the community?

options.A: Firing the nurses and hiring administrative clerks
options.B: Employing polyvalent nurses trained in multiple care areas
options.C: Restricting care strictly to adult male patients
options.D: Closing the clinic until a specialist doctor arrives

explanation: Spot on! Having polyvalent nurses means a small team can safely and confidently handle a wide variety of health needs in the community. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h8)

question: Why would a doctor order a hypotonic fluid like 0.45% Normal Saline?

options.A: To maintain a stable vein without altering any fluid balance
options.B: To rapidly replace large volumes of blood loss from trauma
options.C: To treat severe cellular dehydration by moving water into tissues
options.D: To pull excess fluid out of swollen brain cells and tissues

explanation: Think of hypotonic fluids as having fewer particles than blood. When a patient is super dehydrated, these fluids move out of the veins and into thirsty cells to plump them back up! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h1)

question: What is the very first emergency medication to give someone having a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis)?

options.A: Oral antihistamine
options.B: Epinephrine
options.C: Paracetamol syrup
options.D: Normal saline IV

explanation: Epinephrine is a lifesaver! It works fast to open airways and boost low blood pressure during severe allergic reactions. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T73#GNS214_U1_T73_h8)

question: A patient sits crying silently in bed after receiving a terminal diagnosis. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Turn on the television to distract them from sadness
options.B: Remind them that modern medicine is very advanced
options.C: Leave the room immediately to give them privacy
options.D: Sit quietly beside the patient and offer a reassuring touch

explanation: Offering presence and gentle touch shows support and lets the patient know they are not alone in their grief. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h6)

question: In the ward, what do we mean by an 'adverse event'?

options.A: Harm caused by medical management rather than the disease
options.B: An unavoidable symptom of a natural disease process
options.C: Any emotional stress a patient feels before surgery
options.D: A patient refusing to take prescribed hospital medications

explanation: Spot on! An adverse event means the patient got hurt because of the care or treatment given, not because of their sickness itself. You'll master these safety terms in no time! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T7#GNS312_U5_T7_h1)

question: What is another common medical name for the subcutaneous tissue layer?

options.A: Hypodermis
options.B: Epidermis
options.C: Fascia
options.D: Periosteum

explanation: You got it! 'Hypo' means beneath and 'dermis' refers to the skin, so hypodermis is just another name for the subcutaneous layer right underneath. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the single biggest preventable cause of chronic lung disease (COPD) worldwide?

options.A: Childhood asthma attacks
options.B: Inhaling coal dust at work
options.C: Smoke from indoor cooking fires
options.D: Tobacco smoke exposure

explanation: Tobacco smoke is tough on the airways and air sacs over time. Because people can choose to avoid or quit it, it stands out as the number one preventable cause of COPD globally. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h2)

question: When must a patient come back to have a Mantoux tuberculin skin test read?

options.A: 48 to 72 hours
options.B: 5 to 7 days
options.C: Immediately after injection
options.D: 12 to 24 hours

explanation: Spot on! This 48 to 72-hour window gives the body enough time to build a visible immune reaction for us to measure accurately. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T8#GNS125_U3_T8_h5)

question: Which cranial nerves have their roots located right inside the brain stem?

options.A: Cranial nerves III through XII
options.B: Only the spinal accessory nerve
options.C: All twelve pairs of cranial nerves
options.D: Cranial nerves I and II only

explanation: Ten out of the twelve pairs of cranial nerves (from number three to twelve) actually originate right inside the brain stem. Neat, right? [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h2)

question: Which part of the body is best seen using an MRI scan?

options.A: Free air in the abdomen
options.B: Soft tissues and ligaments
options.C: Hard cortical bone surfaces
options.D: Tiny bone micro-calcifications

explanation: Great job! MRI is a star at showing soft tissues like muscles, tendons, and ligaments because they have a lot of water content. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why should a nurse emphasize that tubal ligation is permanent even though microsurgical reversals exist?

options.A: Reversal operations always cause permanent damage to the ovaries and uterus.
options.B: The human fallopian tubes instantly dissolve once they are surgically cut.
options.C: Reversal surgery is expensive, complex, and has uncertain success rates.
options.D: Hospitals legally forbid patients from ever attempting to reverse the procedure.

explanation: Reversing a tubal ligation requires delicate microsurgery that is not always successful, making it unwise for patients to rely on it as a backup plan. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h7)

question: What do we call it when a nurse physically walks through a factory floor to observe how safe the workers' habits are?

options.A: Financial auditing
options.B: Job safety analysis
options.C: Biological sampling
options.D: Workplace walkthrough

explanation: A workplace walkthrough lets healthcare pros see real working conditions and habits firsthand so we can help keep workers safe. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h5)

question: A patient takes a standard dose of an antibiotic they've used safely before, but suddenly develops a severe skin rash. What type of reaction is this?

options.A: Type A Augmented reaction
options.B: A normal therapeutic response
options.C: Type B Bizarre reaction
options.D: A simple medication overdose

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Type B reactions are unpredictable hypersensitivity or immune responses that don't follow normal dose rules. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h2)

question: Why do clinical trials sometimes miss some side effects before a drug is finally approved?

options.A: Regulatory agencies forbid companies from testing long-term effects
options.B: They involve too few patients and last for a limited time
options.C: Researchers deliberately hide minor side effect data from the public
options.D: Participants in clinical trials never take the correct drug dosage

explanation: Great thinking! Clinical trials only test a small group of people for a short while. Rare or long-term side effects often only show up later when millions of everyday people start taking the drug. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h1)

question: A patient finishing treatment is terrified the cancer will return. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Promise them that cancer never, ever comes back
options.B: Tell them to stop thinking about their health history
options.C: Acknowledge their fear and discuss healthy coping and follow-up plans
options.D: Refer them for emergency surgery immediately

explanation: Fear of a comeback is completely normal for survivors. Validating their feelings and showing them the clear follow-up plan brings real peace of mind. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T9#GNS311_U2_T9_h9)

question: Why would you want to conduct a key informant interview with a respected local elder?

options.A: To test the reading and writing skills of the village leadership
options.B: To force the elder to pay for community health insurance schemes
options.C: To gain deep, expert insights into the community's history and health barriers
options.D: To replace the need for any quantitative surveys in the village

explanation: Correct! Key informants hold valuable local knowledge that helps explain why certain health habits stick around. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is the name of the specific space that directly surrounds and protects the human heart?

options.A: cranial cavity
options.B: pleural cavity
options.C: pericardial cavity
options.D: mediastinum cavity

explanation: Think 'peri' for around and 'cardio' for heart! The pericardial cavity is the cozy, fluid-filled space right around your heart. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the safest thing to do right after giving an injection with a disposable syringe?

options.A: Place the uncapped syringe on the patient's bedside table
options.B: Drop the entire syringe into a nearby sharps container
options.C: Recap the needle firmly using a two-handed technique
options.D: Break the needle off before disposal

explanation: Correct! To avoid accidental needle pricks, always drop the whole sharp device straight into a puncture-resistant container without trying to recap it. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h4)

question: During the rainy season, a community health nurse sees more waterborne illnesses. What is the best immediate community action to prioritize?

options.A: Encouraging families to sleep under insecticide-treated bed nets every night
options.B: Advising community members to avoid all physical contact during greetings
options.C: Promoting daily physical exercise to strengthen cardiovascular endurance
options.D: Educating residents on water purification methods like boiling or chlorination

explanation: You got it! Since waterborne diseases spread through contaminated drinking water, making the water safe to drink is the most direct way to stop them. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T4#GNS313_U1_T4_h4)

question: A patient swallowed a small toy that got stuck in their throat. Why would a doctor perform a laryngoscopy?

options.A: To test the patient's swallowing reflex
options.B: To locate and safely remove the inhaled object
options.C: To measure the oxygen content in the lungs
options.D: To check for chronic bacterial throat infections

explanation: Spot on! When something gets stuck where it shouldn't be, this procedure lets the clinician spot the object and safely take it out. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T4#GNS221_U2_T4_h2)

question: When checking a newborn's spine during a routine exam, what hidden sign might a nurse look for?

options.A: A dimple or tuft of hair over the spine
options.B: How fast the bones are hardening
options.C: Spinal reflex pathways
options.D: Bruises from the delivery process

explanation: Surprise! Little skin clues like a deep dimple or hairy patch right on the lower back can hint at a hidden spinal issue like spina bifida occulta. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h5)

question: What two physical measurements are required to calculate a person's BMI?

options.A: Waist and hip measurements
options.B: Height and skinfold thickness
options.C: Height and weight
options.D: Weight and waist circumference

explanation: The standard BMI calculation relies exclusively on an individual's height and total body weight. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T10#GNS121_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is required before starting a cross-sectional study involving human participants?

options.A: Ethical approval from an institutional review board
options.B: Mandatory participation from every single patient in the city
options.C: Guaranteed financial profit for the hospital ward
options.D: Written permission from international pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Patient safety and rights always come first. You must get proper ethical clearance before involving human subjects in research. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h8)

question: Over which major chest muscle do the breasts primarily rest?

options.A: Intercostal muscle
options.B: Pectoralis major
options.C: Latissimus dorsi
options.D: Rectus abdominis

explanation: The pectoralis major muscle forms the muscular bed directly underneath the breast tissue on the anterior chest wall. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h1)

question: Which body organ must a nurse monitor closely when a patient is on long-term azole antifungal therapy?

options.A: Bone marrow output
options.B: Visual acuity
options.C: Pulmonary function
options.D: Liver function

explanation: Well done! Azole drugs can stress the liver, so checking liver enzyme blood tests regularly is a key part of safe nursing care. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h6)

question: Which hormone is released by the adrenal glands to help raise heart rate and blood pressure during shock?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Thyroxine
options.D: Adrenaline

explanation: The sympathetic nervous system releases adrenaline and noradrenaline to quickly boost heart rate and tighten blood vessels during a crisis. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which of these is a NORMAL finding and NOT a danger sign for a new mother?

options.A: Soaking through two large sanitary pads in one hour
options.B: A high fever with chills
options.C: Mild tiredness after caring for the baby at night
options.D: Sudden severe chest pain and trouble breathing

explanation: Every new mum is tired! But heavy bleeding, chest pain, and high fever are urgent warning signs that need immediate attention. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h6)

question: Which of the following measurements is included in anthropometric assessment?

options.A: Heart rate and rhythm
options.B: Serum albumin levels
options.C: Height and weight
options.D: Blood pressure readings

explanation: Anthropometric measurements involve physical body dimensions such as height, weight, and body mass index. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h6)

question: Which questionnaire is widely used to check different parts of female sexual function?

options.A: Mini-Mental State Examination
options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: Beck Depression Inventory
options.D: Female Sexual Function Index

explanation: You got it! The FSFI is the go-to tool researchers and clinicians use to measure things like desire, arousal, and comfort. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T25#GNS312_U1_T25_h6)

question: A pregnant patient is abandoned by her partner and threatened with rejection by her family. What is she most at risk for?

options.A: Complete physical immunity to pregnancy-related complications
options.B: Severe psychological distress and seeking unsafe abortion options
options.C: Immediate promotion to a leadership position at her workplace
options.D: Instant access to free government housing and welfare

explanation: Spot on. Total isolation without support can push scared patients to take terrible risks. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h6)

question: What valve does blood pass through immediately after leaving the right ventricle?

options.A: Mitral valve
options.B: Aortic semilunar valve
options.C: Pulmonary semilunar valve
options.D: Tricuspid valve

explanation: As the right ventricle contracts, blood pushes open the pulmonary semilunar valve to enter the pulmonary trunk. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h3)

question: Which cranial nerves are attached to the medulla oblongata?

options.A: CN V, VI, VII, and VIII
options.B: CN IX, X, XI, and XII
options.C: CN III, IV, V, and VI
options.D: CN I, II, III, and IV

explanation: The glossopharyngeal, vagus, accessory, and hypoglossal cranial nerves all have their roots emerging from the medulla. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h2)

question: You organize a support group for mothers managing sickle cell anemia across three different towns. What type of community have you formed?

options.A: A geographic community
options.B: A rural farming community
options.C: An urban slum settlement
options.D: A community of interest

explanation: Spot on! Even though they live in different towns, they are united by a common health experience, making them a classic community of interest. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T1#GNS124_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which part of the nervous system takes over during non-REM sleep to slow your heart rate and lower blood pressure?

options.A: Sympathetic nervous system
options.B: Enteric nervous system
options.C: Somatic nervous system
options.D: Parasympathetic nervous system

explanation: The parasympathetic system is your 'rest and digest' mode. It slows things down so your body can conserve energy. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h7)

question: A patient after cancer surgery refuses to get out of bed to walk. What is the best thing to do?

options.A: Allow the patient to stay in bed all day without moving
options.B: Wait until the surgeon arrives before attempting any movement
options.C: Scold the patient for being uncooperative with recovery
options.D: Explain that early walking helps prevent blood clots and lung problems

explanation: Kind patient education works wonders! A gentle explanation helps them see why moving early is vital for preventing serious issues like clots. You've got the nurse's touch! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why is a quick chat with a patient at the bedside considered health education?

options.A: Every clinical interaction is an opportunity to share knowledge
options.B: Patients prefer talking over reading heavy medical textbooks
options.C: Hospital management requires a daily quota of conversations
options.D: It gives the nurse a break from heavy physical tasks

explanation: Exactly! Teaching doesn't only happen in a formal classroom. Even a brief chat while checking vitals helps a patient understand their health better. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which UN number is typically used for routine diagnostic specimens classified as Category B biological substances?
explanation: Think of UN 3373 as the standard code you see on diamond labels for everyday lab samples like blood tubes. Easy to remember once you spot it a few times! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h2)

question: What causes a patient to start having convulsions as asphyxia gets worse?

options.A: Sudden infection spreading to the spinal cord
options.B: Severe lack of oxygen affecting brain function
options.C: A massive release of digestive enzymes
options.D: Rapid cooling of the skin surface

explanation: When brain cells are starved of oxygen for too long, they start misfiring wildly. This erratic electrical activity leads to muscle twitching and convulsions. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T6#GNS221_U3_T6_h2)

question: How does cultural stigma negatively affect persons with physical disabilities?

options.A: It forces government agencies to build more accessible hospitals.
options.B: It improves community participation and social integration.
options.C: It automatically guarantees them high-paying government employment.
options.D: It encourages families to hide affected members away from public view and services.

explanation: Negative cultural views can create unfair shame, leading families to isolate affected members and stopping them from seeking help. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h8)

question: Why is it risky to reuse old prescription drugs for a new sickness?

options.A: The current symptoms may stem from a completely different underlying condition
options.B: Old pills lose their physical shape and become impossible to swallow safely
options.C: Pharmacy laws strictly forbid keeping unused tablets in a home cabinet
options.D: Expired medications always turn into toxic chemical substances immediately

explanation: Just because malaria felt a certain way last month doesn't mean today's fever is malaria! Treating a new problem with old medicine can delay finding the real issue. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h1)

question: A nurse, a pharmacist, and a ward manager need to discuss a complex treatment plan for a critical patient. Which meeting format should they use?

options.A: Hospital board meeting
options.B: Administrative budget briefing
options.C: Multidisciplinary case conference
options.D: General staff handover

explanation: When different health professionals team up for a tricky patient case, it's called a multidisciplinary case conference. [learn more](GST321_U7_T4#GST321_U7_T4_h2)

question: Why do planners analyze medical logs and hospital transport times after an event ends?

options.A: To calculate the exact profit margin of the food vendors
options.B: To determine which medical staff members should receive a salary cut
options.C: To evaluate the effectiveness of the medical response and refine future planning
options.D: To verify that all attendees purchased official merchandise

explanation: Looking at medical records helps planners figure out if they had enough nurses, supplies, or ambulances, making future events even safer. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T3#GNS315_U3_T3_h8)

question: Which hormone do standard pregnancy test strips detect to confirm that implantation has happened?

options.A: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.B: Basal testosterone
options.C: Luteinizing hormone
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: You nailed it! hCG is produced by the newly implanted cells and shows up in blood and urine, making it the classic marker on pregnancy tests. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T2#GNS121_U6_T2_h5)

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to check a patient's medication chart before interpreting a U&E result?

options.A: Medications interfere with the physical color of blood plasma
options.B: Certain drugs directly alter electrolyte and kidney function values
options.C: Hospital policy requires a drug screen with every blood draw
options.D: Drugs alter the patient's total blood volume instantly

explanation: Exactly! Many everyday drugs—like blood pressure meds and water pills—can directly push sodium and potassium up or down. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T9#GNS123_U2_T9_h5)

question: A public health nurse is tracking down everyone who spent time near a patient with an active bacterial infection. What is this nursing action called?

options.A: Vector control
options.B: Environmental sterilization
options.C: Active immunization
options.D: Contact tracing

explanation: Brilliant! This is a core public health nursing duty. Tracing contacts helps us find everyone who might have caught the bug and stops the transmission chain right in its tracks. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T3#GNS313_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why do estrogen levels drop heavily as the ovaries age?

options.A: The liver breaks down estrogen faster than normal
options.B: The remaining ovarian follicles become unresponsive to stimulation
options.C: The adrenal glands block the synthesis of steroid hormones
options.D: The pituitary gland stops making gonadotropins entirely

explanation: Since the follicles inside the ovaries are what make estrogen, losing their responsiveness means estrogen levels naturally fall. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T15#GNS121_U5_T15_h2)

question: What is the golden rule of fluid balance when it comes to sodium?

options.A: Sodium ignores fluid shifts
options.B: Water follows sodium
options.C: Sodium follows protein
options.D: Water pushes sodium out

explanation: You got it! Think of sodium as a magnet—wherever sodium goes, water is definitely going to follow it. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T008#GNS227_U6_T008_h2)

question: When calculating an incidence rate, what goes into the denominator (the bottom number)?

options.A: The total number of deaths recorded in the hospital
options.B: The total budget allocated for public health programs
options.C: The number of patients who have already recovered
options.D: The total population at risk of getting the disease

explanation: When calculating rates, your denominator must only include people who can actually catch the disease. Makes complete sense when you think about it! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h4)

question: A patient facing severe financial hardship asks you about family planning. What is her money constraint most likely to affect?

options.A: Her natural immunity against common infections
options.B: Her ability to consistently buy and use modern contraceptives
options.C: Her biological response to hormonal medications
options.D: Her genetic predisposition to chronic illnesses

explanation: That's right! Money worries directly affect purchasing power, making it tough to afford steady supplies of birth control. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h2)

question: Which nitrogenous base always pairs with Adenine in a DNA molecule?

options.A: Uracil
options.B: Thymine
options.C: Guanine
options.D: Cytosine

explanation: Adenine always bonds specifically with thymine to form the rungs of the DNA ladder. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h1)

question: Approximately what percentage of a person's vulnerability to addiction is typically attributed to genetics?

options.A: Nearly 100 percent
options.B: Around 10 percent
options.C: About 50 percent
options.D: Less than 5 percent

explanation: Twin and family studies consistently show that genetic predisposition accounts for about half of a person's risk for developing an addiction. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why does MBO help improve staff morale in a nursing unit?

options.A: Because supervisors stop visiting the clinical areas
options.B: Because salaries are automatically doubled every month
options.C: Because nurses have a voice in setting their targets
options.D: Because it removes all heavy workloads from the ward

explanation: Involving staff in decision-making gives them a sense of ownership, which boosts workplace morale. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the main goal of recommending an anti-inflammatory diet, like the Mediterranean diet, in psychiatric care?

options.A: To force the body to rapidly lose large amounts of water weight
options.B: To cure genetic disorders within a few weeks of starting
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for any prescription medications
options.D: To reduce systemic inflammation that negatively impacts brain function

explanation: Correct! Lowering bodily inflammation helps support optimal brain health and can ease depressive symptoms. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h6)

question: A patient had a right-sided mastectomy last year. Which arm should you use for venepuncture?

options.A: On the right arm
options.B: On the left arm
options.C: In the right hand veins only
options.D: Either arm without preference

explanation: Always avoid the arm on the side of a previous mastectomy because lymph flow there is compromised, making infections much harder to fight off. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is an early or forced marriage?

options.A: Any wedding that takes place without religious approval
options.B: A marital arrangement organized strictly by government officials
options.C: A union where one or both parties are under 18 without full consent
options.D: Any marriage occurring between individuals from different tribes

explanation: Spot on! Early and forced marriage means minors are pushed into a union without giving free and wise personal consent. As nurses, protecting the young is key! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T13#GNS312_U1_T13_h1)

question: What is an important task for school management when evaluating their health programme?

options.A: Reviewing clinic attendance logs to spot health trends
options.B: Changing the academic grading system every term
options.C: Firing teachers who report sick with malaria
options.D: Keeping all student medical records strictly secret from staff

explanation: Exactly! Checking clinic records helps leaders spot recurring health issues early and take quick, smart action. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h7)

question: A patient is healing from a major surgery and needs help repairing skin and tissues. Which nutrient should you encourage?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Saturated fats
options.C: Simple starches
options.D: Proteins

explanation: Well done! Surgical wounds need plenty of protein to rebuild skin, muscle, and internal structures back to health. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h2)

question: Which of the following is a direct consequence of failing to record items taken from the ward inventory?

options.A: The medications on the shelf will expire much faster than normal
options.B: The hospital will automatically order double the amount needed
options.C: Patients will recover faster because fewer drugs are logged
options.D: Stock counts will not match actual inventory, causing unexpected shortages

explanation: Unrecorded items create hidden inventory gaps, making reorder calculations inaccurate and leading to sudden stockouts. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h6)

question: Which simple tool kit helps a nurse look clearly inside a patient's mouth?

options.A: A penlight and a tongue depressor
options.B: A flexible urinary catheter tube
options.C: A sterile lumbar puncture needle
options.D: A heavy metal reflex hammer

explanation: Keep it simple and practical! A penlight gives you light, and a tongue depressor helps you gently see every corner of the oral cavity. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h3)

question: What is a major reason food gets lost before it ever reaches the local market?

options.A: Excessive consumer demand in urban centers
options.B: High levels of crop diversity on small farms
options.C: Poor storage facilities and bad transport roads
options.D: Strict government food safety inspections

explanation: Bad roads and poor storage mean a lot of harvest spoils before getting to people who need it. A very real challenge in many regions! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T021#GNS227_U2_T021_h2)

question: Which behavior from a nurse will immediately make a teenager shut down and stop talking?

options.A: Listening actively to the patient's concerns
options.B: Maintaining a calm and welcoming facial expression
options.C: Asking simple open-ended questions
options.D: Displaying a judgmental or scolding attitude

question: Why is it so important for young neurons to migrate to new locations in the developing brain?

options.C: It ensures the recommended treatment is realistic for their daily life
options.D: It prevents family members from visiting the ward

explanation: Brilliant! Knowing what life looks like at home helps us design treatment plans the patient can actually afford and manage. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T6#GNS312_U4_T6_h7)

question: A nurse fills out a Yellow Form for a patient who got a rash after taking two new drugs and an herbal supplement. What should be included in the medication history?

options.A: Only document the drug that the nurse personally administered
options.B: List all prescribed drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal products
options.C: Ignore the herbal supplement since it is not a pharmaceutical drug
options.D: Only list the most expensive brand-name prescription drug

explanation: Always list everything! Herbal remedies and over-the-counter items frequently cause or contribute to adverse reactions. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why is assessing family dynamics an important first step for a nurse?

options.A: It determines the exact date the patient contracted the virus
options.B: It helps identify who can serve as the primary care partner
options.C: It proves whether the family has a history of viral infections
options.D: It legally binds the family to pay for all future drugs

explanation: Brilliant! Understanding relationships inside the home helps the nurse find the most supportive relative to assist with care. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T6#GNS216_U6_T6_h7)

question: A patient insists that their mother, who passed away years ago, is coming to visit today. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Argue firmly that the mother is dead to teach them reality
options.B: Scold the family members for not correcting the patient's false memory
options.C: Ignore the comment completely and pretend you did not hear anything
options.D: Acknowledge the feeling behind the statement and gently redirect their attention

explanation: Argueing causes distress. Instead, validate their emotion ('You really miss your mum, don't you?') and gently steer their focus elsewhere. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T10#GNS324_U4_T10_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of non-verbal communication that can significantly influence a patient interaction?

options.A: The specific medical terminology used in the care plan
options.B: Open posture and relaxed facial expressions
options.C: A printed schedule of clinic operating hours
options.D: The speed at which discharge instructions are read aloud

explanation: Body language, posture, and facial expressions are non-verbal cues that convey openness, empathy, or disinterest without using words. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h2)

question: What is the primary role of laboratory reports in microbial surveillance?

options.A: Tracking patient dietary preferences
options.B: Identifying pathogens and their drug sensitivities
options.C: Recording the financial cost of hospital stays
options.D: Scheduling nurse shifts on the hospital ward

explanation: Labs confirm the exact germ causing the illness and check which drugs can kill it. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h4)

question: Why is it so dangerous to mix sleeping pills with alcohol?

options.A: It causes immediate and irreversible liver failure within one hour
options.B: It neutralizes the medication, rendering the patient completely sleepless
options.C: It leads to profound respiratory depression and coma due to additive central nervous system suppression
options.D: It triggers severe high blood pressure and sudden stroke

explanation: Both alcohol and sleeping pills slow down your brain. Mixing them doubles up that depressing effect, which can easily stop a person's breathing. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T1#GNS223_U6_T1_h5)

question: Which condition means a patient must NEVER be given misoprostol?

options.A: Well-managed gestational diabetes
options.B: Mild iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: A history of high blood pressure
options.D: A confirmed ectopic pregnancy

explanation: Misoprostol cannot treat a pregnancy outside the uterus. Giving it would dangerously delay emergency surgery. Always check for this first! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h3)

question: What does cross-contamination mean in food safety?

options.A: The accidental freezing of fresh vegetables in the refrigerator
options.B: The mixing of two different dry grains in the same storage bin
options.C: The transfer of harmful germs from raw food to ready-to-eat food
options.D: The change in food color due to exposure to bright sunlight

explanation: Cross-contamination happens when bacteria move from raw items (like meat) to food you're about to eat without cooking. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h6)

question: Why do daily wage earners find it difficult to attend primary healthcare clinics during the day?

options.A: Clinics refuse to treat people who work in the informal sector
options.B: Transportation is completely unavailable during daytime hours
options.C: Doctors only consult patients during the night
options.D: They lose a day of critical income while waiting at the hospital

explanation: Long daytime waiting hours present a direct financial penalty for men who depend on daily wages to survive. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h5)
